To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
virtual human agents that use first person autobiographical stories can increase user engagement and enjoyment without significantly increasing perceptions of agent deceit.

(1) users enjoyed interactions with an agent more when the agent told stories about itself, rather than about other people, even though users rated the agent as being dishonest in both conditions, and (2) users were more likely to complete conversations with the agent when it told stories about itself rather than about others.

1) users enjoy interacting more with a virtual human who presents a first person back story compared to a third person back story, but 2) users do not perceive the virtual human to be more dishonest when it presents the first person back story.

the design and evaluation of virtual humans who tell stories about their lives to engage and retain users.
the development of virtual humans that engage with users in meaningful and enjoyable ways, and with the ethical implications of presenting human autobiographies as the virtual human’s own.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

presenting the agent's stories as the agent's own history (first person) was more enjoyable and engaging for users than presenting them as stories of other humans (third person), but that users in both conditions rated the agent as being equally dishonest in the stories it told.

the use of a back story in a virtual human can be effective at increasing engagement with users and that this effect can be achieved with a first-person back story without increasing user perceptions of dishonesty.
the use of a first person back story is an effective method of increasing user engagement with a virtual human, and is an ethically acceptable approach to developing virtual humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
it is possible to use a virtual human with an autobiographical back story to promote engagement with the user and to increase user exercise.
virtual humans can be more engaging and persuasive if they are able to relate their fictitious personal experiences, and that this can be accomplished without raising concerns of dishonesty.

virtual humans can be designed to present fictitious autobiographical stories that users perceive as honest, and that these stories can be used to maintain user interaction and retention in a virtual agent intervention.
The main takeaway from our work is that

it is possible to create a virtual human that can engage users with a human-like back story without being perceived as dishonest, and that such agents may be able to promote long term engagement with users.
the use of a virtual human with human autobiographies can be a viable and effective way to maintain engagement with users and to promote user retention in interventions.
virtual humans can effectively use personal stories to maintain user engagement in an intervention, and that users may be more engaged when the virtual human tells stories in first person.
